run_guide.summary: Get the published benchmark tables, and score new multi-residue variants with the repository's command-line tool.
prerequisites: Python with tqdm, numpy, pandas, biopython, torch and fair-esm, as the README's install line lists.
The ESM1b weights, which fair-esm downloads; the README notes the model comes from Meta AI's official repository.
For scoring a new set, a CSV with wt_seq, mut_seq and start_pos columns.
The code is MIT licensed. ClinVar labels are public; the HGMD part of the wider paper is not, but neither of these two benchmarks uses it.

steps.title: Get the code and the published benchmarks
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/ntranoslab/esm-variants.git
cd esm-variants
git checkout --detach 0c33758a5073e5d6e673d9a16a40e5b0af46851d
steps.explanation: The clone and cd lines are the README's; the checkout line was added here to pin the commit these steps were read from. The clone brings down the indel and stop-gain benchmark tables, which already contain every compared method's scores.

steps.title: Install the dependencies
steps.shell: pip3 install tqdm numpy pandas biopython torch fair-esm
steps.explanation: The one install line the README gives.

steps.title: Score multi-residue variants
steps.shell: python3 esm_score_multi_residue_mutations.py --input-csv-file /path/to/input.csv --output-csv-file /path/to/output.csv
steps.explanation: The README's command for in-frame indels and other multi-residue changes. The input CSV needs wt_seq, mut_seq and start_pos; the wild-type and mutated sequences for every variant in the indel benchmark are already columns of the published table.
steps.source_locator: Repository: README.md, Usage; the indel benchmark table header

steps.title: Score all missense substitutions, the route used for stop gains
steps.shell: python3 esm_score_missense_mutations.py --input-fasta-file /path/to/input.fasta --output-csv-file /path/to/output.csv
steps.explanation: The README's other command. A stop-gain score in the paper is the lowest of the missense log-likelihood ratios over the region lost after the new stop codon, so this is the script that produces the underlying scores; the paper does not publish a command that performs that minimisation.
steps.source_locator: Repository: README.md, Usage. Paper: Fig. 6 legend

outputs: A CSV of effect scores for the variants given, written to the path passed to the script.
The cloned repository's benchmark tables, which already hold the ESM1b, CADD and baseline scores for the 3,470 indels and the stop-gain set, plus Table_of_results.xlsx.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
No published command computes the reported ROC-AUCs, the permutation tests or the bootstrapped error bars; the repository publishes the scored tables and the scoring tools only.

The stop-gain pipeline is not a single command: the minimisation over missense scores in the lost region and the 50 base pair partition are described in the paper, not shipped as a script in the files read.

description: Zero-shot classification of human variants from ClinVar, SpliceVarDB and BRCA1/BRCA2 functional assays, scored with Evo 2 and comparison models by the Evo 2 authors; AUROC and AUPRC per variant stratum in Supplementary Data 1.

attributes.task: Classify pathogenic or loss-of-function human variants from benign or functional variants by zero-shot model scores
attributes.scope_note: Protocols are the variant strata of Supplementary Data 1; one evaluation per model and stratum.

profile.summary: This is the human variant effect evaluation in the Evo 2 paper, not a released benchmark suite. The authors scored ClinVar variants, SpliceVarDB splice variants and BRCA1 and BRCA2 functional assay variants zero-shot with Evo 2 and a range of comparison models, and report AUROC and AUPRC per variant stratum. It is useful for seeing how a DNA language model compares with conservation scores, protein language models and supervised predictors on coding, noncoding, SNV and non-SNV variants.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Human variant effect prediction, Fig. 3 legend; SI: A.3.12 to A.3.15

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a model's zero-shot score separates harmful from harmless human variants. Four label sources are used: ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic versus benign or likely benign; SpliceVarDB experimentally validated splice-altering variants; BRCA1 saturation genome editing classes (loss of function versus functional or intermediate); and BRCA2 functional classifications. ClinVar results are split into coding and noncoding, SNV and non-SNV, by phyloP conservation bin and by distance from splice sites, so the evaluation also covers insertions, deletions and other non-SNVs that many predictors cannot score.
sections.source_locator: SI: A.3.13 to A.3.15; Paper: Human variant effect prediction

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: ClinVar is the October 2024 release, restricted to nuclear variants with at least two review stars, with variants of unknown significance removed and variants affecting more than 64 bp of reference or alternate sequence removed. SpliceVarDB variants labelled low frequency are excluded. BRCA1 and BRCA2 labels are the classes assigned in the original assay studies: for BRCA1, 823 loss-of-function SNVs against 3,070 functional or intermediate SNVs; for BRCA2, 1,156 against 5,681. All models score the same variants within each benchmark.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Each variant is scored zero-shot as the change in log-likelihood between the variant and reference sequence; a more negative change means more deleterious. Evo 2 scores an 8,192 bp genomic window around the variant. Encoder models use masked marginal likelihood for SNVs and the change in pseudolikelihood for non-SNVs; PhyloP non-SNV scores average the affected positions; Pangolin uses the largest absolute predicted change in splice site usage. Classification is scored with AUROC and AUPRC per stratum. The full per-model, per-stratum results are in Supplementary Data 1. A separate supervised BRCA1 experiment trains ridge regression on Evo 2 embeddings with a position-grouped 80/20 split; it is not part of the zero-shot comparison.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: ClinVar October 2024 (coding: 14,319 SNVs and 1,236 non-SNVs; noncoding: 34,761 SNVs and 3,894 non-SNVs), SpliceVarDB (1,181 exonic and 3,769 intronic variants), BRCA1 saturation genome editing SNVs (3,893; 2,077 coding and 1,125 noncoding) and BRCA2 functional SNVs (1,156 loss of function and 5,681 functional or intermediate).
facts.source_locator: Paper: Fig. 3 legend; SI: A.3.15

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: No train or test split for the zero-shot comparison: all variants are evaluation data. The separate supervised BRCA1 experiment splits 1,326 genomic positions 80/20 into 3,104 training and 789 test SNVs.

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: AUROC and AUPRC per stratum; higher is better.

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: PhyloP (100, 241, 447 and 470 way), ESM models, Nucleotide Transformer, CodonBert, Decodon, EnCodon, RNA-FM, AlphaMissense, GPN-MSA, SpliceAI, Pangolin and CADD, each on the strata it can score.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: No variant-level control is described for comparison models. For Evo 2, the authors state it was not trained on human genetic variation or functional genomics data. Supervised comparators such as CADD, SpliceAI and Pangolin may have been trained on overlapping labels; the sources do not address this.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Human variant effect prediction, final paragraph

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Unreported: the sections read give point AUROC and AUPRC values without confidence intervals or replicates.

facts.label: Entity type
facts.value: A human genetic variant (SNV, insertion, deletion or multi-nucleotide variant).

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: Human.

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Clinical classifications (ClinVar), experimentally validated splicing effects (SpliceVarDB) and functional scores from BRCA1 saturation mutagenesis and BRCA2 experimental measurements.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Human variant effect prediction; SI: A.3.15

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: DNA models read the genomic sequence around the variant; protein models read the gene's amino acid sequence; conservation and supervised predictors use their own inputs.

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Zero-shot likelihood scoring for the main comparison; one supplementary experiment trains a ridge regression probe on Evo 2 embeddings for BRCA1.

strengths.text: Covers non-SNV variants (insertions, deletions, multi-nucleotide variants) as well as SNVs, and noncoding as well as coding regions.
Within each benchmark all models score the same variants, and ClinVar results are stratified by conservation and splice-site distance.
Uses functional assay labels (BRCA1, BRCA2, SpliceVarDB) alongside clinical labels.

limitations.text: It is one paper's evaluation, run by the Evo 2 authors. No scoring code for the full comparison is listed in the availability statements, only the Evo 2 repository with an example BRCA1 notebook. Supplementary Data 1 is described as scores and metadata for the human variant effect prediction analysis; it was not read for this page.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Code availability; Supplementary information list; evo2 README: Notebooks

limitations.text: Comparison models cover different subsets: GPN-MSA and AlphaMissense cannot score non-SNVs, so some strata compare fewer methods.

BRCA1 intermediate (INT) variants are merged with functional variants, and BRCA1 and BRCA2 labels come from thresholds set in the original assay studies, so the task is binary even where the assay is graded.
The article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so the text cannot be redistributed in modified form or commercially.

profile.summary: The variant effect benchmarks used in the GPN-MSA paper to test unsupervised deleteriousness scores on the human genome. They pit ClinVar pathogenic, COSMIC frequent and OMIM regulatory variants against common gnomAD variants, test enrichment of rare over common gnomAD variants among the most deleterious scores, and add ProteinGym DMS and DepMap gene essentiality. They are for comparing DNA language models with conservation scores, CADD and protein models on coding and non-coding variants.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a score ranks deleterious human variants above neutral ones without being trained on human variant labels. Coding variants are tested through ClinVar, COSMIC and DMS; non-coding through OMIM regulatory variants and gnomAD; gene-level through DepMap essentiality.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Results

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: ClinVar release 20230730; COSMIC MutantCensus v98 with frequency computed from whole-genome or whole-exome samples; a curated OMIM set of pathogenic regulatory variants; gnomAD 3.1.2 filtered to allele number of at least 25000 with common variants above 5% MAF and rare variants as singletons; ProteinGym v0.1 human DMS data; DepMap Public 23Q4 gene dependency. OMIM variants are matched to gnomAD common variants by regulatory category. The ablation set subsamples rare variants to match common variants per consequence. The labelled ClinVar, COSMIC, OMIM and gnomAD sets are published on Hugging Face.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Each method gives one score per variant (for GPN-MSA, the log-likelihood ratio of alternate to reference, averaged over strands). ClinVar is scored by AUROC; COSMIC, OMIM and DepMap by AUPRC; gnomAD by the odds ratio of rare to common variants in the deleterious tail, with the tail set by allowing about 30 false discoveries and p-values from a one-sided Fisher's exact test. DMS sets are binarised with ProteinGym cut-offs, except TADBP, where a 0.125 cut-off on absolute relative toxicity is used. Some expensive models were scored only on ClinVar or part of OMIM.

name: Zero-shot cell embedding evaluation of single-cell foundation models (Kedzierska et al. 2025)
description: Zero-shot cell embeddings from scGPT (four variants) and Geneformer compared with 2,000 highly variable genes, Harmony and scVI on five human scRNA-seq datasets, scored for cell-type separation and batch mixing with scIB metrics, plus a check of each model's pretraining reconstruction objective.

attributes.task: Zero-shot cell embedding for cell-type clustering and batch integration
attributes.scope_note: Five datasets (Pancreas, PBMC 12k, PBMC 95k, Immune, Tabula Sapiens) plus a Pancreas (8k) row; foundation models used without training, baselines fitted on each dataset.
attributes.source_locator: Pages 3-5 'Results and discussion'; pages 7-10 'Methods'; Additional file 1

profile.summary: A single paper's test of whether the cell embeddings of scGPT and Geneformer are useful without any further training (zero-shot). Embeddings are scored on five human single-cell RNA-seq datasets for separating known cell types and for mixing batches, against 2,000 highly variable genes, Harmony and scVI; a third analysis checks how well each model performs its own pretraining reconstruction task. It is for researchers deciding whether to use a single-cell foundation model's embeddings directly, without fine-tuning.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Results and discussion; Methods

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: The study asks whether single-cell foundation models produce cell embeddings that work without task-specific training, which matters in exploratory work where labels are unknown and fine-tuning is not possible. It scores three things: how well the embedding separates known cell types, how well it removes batch effects while keeping biology, and how well each model performs its own masked-language-model pretraining task of reconstructing gene expression.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Background; Results and discussion

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Five human datasets are used: Pancreas (16k cells, 14 labels, 6 batches, combining 5 studies), PBMC 12k (9 labels, 2 batches), PBMC 95k (10 labels, 1 batch), a cross-tissue Immune atlas (330k cells, 45 labels, 12 batches) and Tabula Sapiens (483k cells, 177 labels, 27 batches). The models are Geneformer and four scGPT variants: randomly initialised, and pretrained on kidney, blood and bone marrow, or whole-human data. Baselines are 2,000 highly variable genes (HVG), and scVI and Harmony trained on each dataset. Some evaluation data were seen in pretraining: part of Pancreas (GEO GSE84133) by Geneformer, and Tabula Sapiens and Immune by scGPT. The authors scored both the full Pancreas set and its non-overlapping subset and report that results were consistent.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Methods 'Models and baselines' and 'Datasets'; Additional file 1 sheets TableS1 and TableS2

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Scoring largely follows Luecken et al. (scIB, version 1.0.4). Cell-type separation uses the average silhouette width (ASW) and AvgBIO, the mean of ASW, NMI and ARI, with NMI and ARI computed on Louvain clusters at the best of 20 resolutions. Batch mixing uses a batch integration score (silhouette with respect to batch, averaged across cell types, subtracted from 1) and the principal component regression (PCR) score; their mean is the Average Batch Score. All scores are on a 0 to 1 scale, higher is better. Scores are computed on the full embedding dimensions and again after UMAP projection. For reconstruction, all genes are left unmasked; scGPT is scored by mean squared error against a mean-prediction baseline and Geneformer by Pearson correlation between true and predicted rankings against an average-ranking baseline.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Methods 'Evaluation metrics', 'Biological preservation scores', 'Batch mixing scores', 'Reconstructing gene expression'; Code availability

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The README's quick start clones the repository, downloads a data archive from figshare, and starts a Jupyter server in the published Docker image. The evaluation is run from three notebooks: one for scGPT, one for Geneformer and one for the HVG and scVI baselines. The code needs an NVIDIA GPU because scGPT requires flash-attention.

limitations.text: Some evaluation datasets were in the models' pretraining data, which the authors say confounds whether trends are general or due to prior exposure.
Only two model families and five transcriptomic datasets are tested; the authors say the datasets do not represent all applications of single-cell analysis.

The comparison is not like for like: baselines are trained on each target dataset and use batch labels, while foundation models are used zero-shot without batch labels. The authors chose this set-up deliberately.

There is no leaderboard or standard submission format; evaluation runs through notebooks that need an NVIDIA GPU, and the README's overview names only scVI and HVG as baselines although the paper also uses Harmony.

name: Perturbation-target prediction from attention-derived edge scores (Kendiukhov 2026, Objective B)
description: For each CRISPR perturbation, score every other gene by an edge score to the perturbed gene (attention, Spearman correlation) or by a gene-level statistic (variance, mean expression, dropout rate), and measure AUROC for classifying the differentially expressed targets. Incremental-value tests add edge scores to a gene-level logistic regression.

attributes.task: Predict which genes are differentially expressed after a CRISPRi or CRISPRa perturbation
attributes.scope_note: Replogle genome-scale CRISPRi (K562, RPE1) and a K562 CRISPRa dataset; T cell and iPSC neuron sets have n = 7 perturbations and print no AUROC values.
attributes.source_locator: Pages 4 and 7-10, 'Results'; pages 13-14, 'Methods'

profile.summary: This is one paper's evaluation, not a released suite. For each gene knocked down or activated in a CRISPR screen, every other gene is scored by its link to the perturbed gene, either an attention weight taken from a single-cell foundation model or a Spearman correlation, and the score is used to classify which genes turn out to be differentially expressed. Performance is the per-perturbation area under the ROC curve. The same test is run for three univariate gene-level features, variance, mean expression and dropout rate, and then a conditional test asks whether adding a pairwise edge score to those gene-level features improves prediction. The answer the paper reports is no: gene-level features reach 0.81 to 0.88 against about 0.70 for either edge type, and adding edges changes the area under the curve by about nothing. The evaluation is useful as a sanity check that anyone claiming regulatory signal in attention has to pass.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation and No incremental pairwise value sections; Methods, Perturbation-first validation and Confound decomposition

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: The paper calls this Objective B, and keeps it apart from Objective A, which is recovery of curated regulatory interactions. Objective B asks whether a pairwise score between a perturbed gene and another gene predicts that the other gene will be differentially expressed after the perturbation. The author stresses that this is an effect-magnitude question, mixing direct regulation, indirect propagation and how detectable a gene is at all, so the two objectives can disagree: a true direct edge may produce little differential expression, and a non-regulatory feature can score well if it proxies target susceptibility. The evaluation therefore sets a floor rather than a ceiling, that any claimed pairwise regulatory signal must first beat features computed from single genes.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, Evaluation framework section; Results, Perturbation-first validation

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The expression data are published CRISPR screens, taken through the scperturb package according to the code repository: the Replogle genome-scale CRISPRi screens in K562, described in the paper as more than 640,000 K562 cells and 2,024 perturbed genes, and in RPE1, Adamson CRISPRa in K562 with 77 perturbations, Tian iPSC neurons with 7, and Shifrut primary T cells with 7. Tabula Sapiens tissues and a brain data set are used for the other objective. Preprocessing is standard Scanpy quality control, genes in at least 3 cells, cells with at least 200 genes, normalisation to 10,000 counts and a log transform, with highly variable gene selection. Labels come from the screens themselves: for each perturbation, a Mann-Whitney test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and a log fold change threshold marks which genes are differentially expressed. The pairwise scores being tested are attention weights from Geneformer V2-316M, averaged over heads within a layer and then over cells, and Spearman correlation edges computed from the same control cells, with absolute value taken because the sign is not comparable. The evaluation universe is 2,000 highly variable genes for K562 and 3,309 for RPE1, where the perturbed genes are forced into the set.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Models and data, Attention extraction, Perturbation-first validation; README.md: Perturbation Datasets, External Data

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Two layers of test. The first is per-perturbation area under the ROC curve: rank all candidate genes for one perturbation by the score under test and ask how well that ranking separates the differentially expressed genes, then compare score types across perturbations with paired tests. On K562 CRISPRi, correlation edges reach 0.696 under the primary settings with 151 perturbations, and all 27 sensitivity conditions give 0.62 to 0.76; Geneformer attention at layer 13 reaches 0.704 on 280 evaluable perturbations, indistinguishable from correlation at 0.703. Variance alone reaches 0.881. The second test is conditional: a data set of 280 by 1,999 perturbation and gene observations, 559,720 pairs with a 2.8 per cent positive rate, five logistic regression models under 5-fold GroupKFold cross validation grouped by perturbation. Gene-level features alone reach 0.895, adding attention changes the area under the curve by minus 0.0004 and adding correlation by minus 0.002. Harder splits were also tried, GroupKFold by target gene and joint gene by perturbation splits, with gradient boosted trees as well as logistic regression and with AUPRC and top-k recall as well as AUROC. Propensity matching, five differential-expression-negative targets matched to each positive one on mean, variance and dropout rate, gives 59,153 matched pairs in which attention retains 0.609 raw discriminability but zero incremental value. All tests use Benjamini-Hochberg correction at 0.05, and bootstrap intervals resample at the perturbation level. A synthetic positive control with a planted network shows the same pipeline detects a real pairwise signal, reporting a change in area under the curve of plus 0.518 in the cleanest variant.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation, No incremental pairwise value and Positive control sections; Methods, Perturbation-first validation, Confound decomposition and Statistical framework

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The analysis code is published as a repository, archived on Zenodo. Create the conda environment from the file in src, let the scperturb package download the perturbation data, and run the module scripts: one for the perturbation-first validation and the trivial baselines, another for the RPE1 confound battery. The repository says each module is self-contained, loads data from external sources or precomputed checkpoints in results, and writes outputs back into results, with resume support. Geneformer weights come from Hugging Face. The licence statement asks anyone wanting to reuse the repository to contact the author first.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Published CRISPR perturbation screens, obtained through scperturb: Replogle K562 CRISPRi, described as more than 640,000 cells and 2,024 perturbed genes, with 280 perturbations evaluable in the attention comparison and 151 under the primary correlation parameterisation; Replogle RPE1 CRISPRi, 1,251 evaluable perturbations and 1,167 in the confound battery, 3,838,263 gene-pair observations; Adamson K562 CRISPRa, 77 perturbations; Tian iPSC neurons, 7; Shifrut primary T cells, 7. The K562 incremental-value table has 280 by 1,999 perturbation and gene observations, 559,720 pairs.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation, No incremental pairwise value, Cross-context and RPE1 sections; README.md: Perturbation Datasets

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Cross validation over perturbations, not a fixed train and test release. The main incremental-value test uses 5-fold GroupKFold grouped by perturbation, so a perturbation's pairs sit entirely in one fold. Harder protocols group by target gene, to stop a gene's own propensity leaking between folds, and combine both into a joint cross-gene by cross-perturbation split. A nested cross-validation protocol is used when choosing the best Geneformer layer out of 18. The primary evaluation layer, layer 13, was fixed in advance from a separate brain data set before any K562 perturbation data were examined.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Confound decomposition; Results, Perturbation-first validation and No incremental pairwise value

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Per-perturbation AUROC for classifying differentially expressed genes, higher is better, is the primary measure. The conditional test reports the change in AUROC from adding an edge score to the gene-level model, with bootstrap confidence intervals, and the harder protocols also report AUPRC and top-k recall. Paired comparisons use Wilcoxon tests and Cohen's d.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Evaluation framework and No incremental pairwise value; Methods, Statistical framework

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: Three univariate gene-level features, expression variance, mean expression and dropout rate, plus Spearman correlation edges computed from the same control cells. On K562, the gene-level features reach 0.81 to 0.88 against about 0.70 for attention and correlation, with variance alone at 0.881, and the gene-level logistic model reaches 0.895. On RPE1 the figures are variance 0.866, mean expression 0.851, dropout 0.797, attention 0.747, correlation 0.658, with the gene-level model at 0.942.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation and Cross-cell-type generalisation

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Several, and they are the point of the design. Cross validation is grouped by perturbation, and in the harder protocols by target gene, so a gene's own susceptibility cannot leak across folds. Propensity matching pairs each differentially expressed target with five non-targets of similar mean, variance and dropout rate, which removes the gene-level advantage before the edge score is judged. Cross-fitted residualisation removes expression covariates from the edge scores. The primary layer was chosen on an independent data set before the perturbation data were seen. There is no control for the perturbation data having been in the foundation models' pretraining corpora.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Confound decomposition; Results, No incremental pairwise value

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Bootstrap confidence intervals with 200 iterations, resampled at the perturbation level unless stated otherwise, reported for the changes in AUROC. Paired p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg correction at 0.05 across a declared family of 95 confirmatory tests out of 153 in all. A power statement is given for the main null: 559,720 observations give more than 99 per cent power to detect a change in AUROC of 0.005.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Statistical framework; Results, No incremental pairwise value

facts.label: Entity type
facts.value: A perturbation and gene pair. One example is one candidate gene considered for one perturbed gene, labelled by whether that gene is differentially expressed after the perturbation. The per-perturbation metric then averages over perturbations, each of which contributes a ranking of all other genes.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation and No incremental pairwise value

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: Human. The cells are human lines and primary human cells: K562, RPE1 retinal epithelial cells, induced pluripotent stem cell derived neurons and primary T cells, with human tissue atlases used for the other objective.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Cross-context replication; README.md: Perturbation Datasets

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Pooled CRISPR screens read out by single-cell RNA sequencing: CRISPRi knockdown in K562, RPE1, neurons and T cells, and CRISPRa activation in K562. The labels are differential expression calls made from those screens with a Mann-Whitney test, Benjamini-Hochberg correction and a log fold change threshold.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Perturbation-first validation; README.md: Perturbation Datasets

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Control cell expression, and a model's internals. The attention scores are extracted from unperturbed cells by forward hooks on each self-attention module, averaged over heads and cells; the correlation scores come from the same control cells; the gene-level features are statistics of the same expression matrix. The perturbed cells are used only to make the labels.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Attention extraction and edge score computation, Perturbation-first validation

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Zero-shot for the foundation models, with a small supervised classifier on top of the features. The published checkpoints are read as they are, Geneformer V2-316M and V1-10M and the scGPT whole-human checkpoint, with no fine-tuning; what is fitted is the logistic regression or gradient boosted model that combines gene-level features and edge scores under cross validation.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Models and data, Confound decomposition

strengths.text: It makes the baseline do the work. Three features computable from the expression matrix alone, variance, mean and dropout rate, are run through the same pipeline, and they beat both edge types, which turns a vague claim about attention into a measurable comparison.

The null result is backed by a sensitivity check of the pipeline itself. On synthetic data with a planted network, and with expression z-scored so univariate variance carries no information about the truth, the same incremental-value test finds a change in AUROC of plus 0.518, and a shuffled control gives nearly zero.

The confounds are attacked from more than one side: grouped cross validation, harder cross-gene and joint splits, linear and nonlinear models, three metrics, residualisation of expression covariates and propensity matching, and the conclusion is the same each time.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Results, No incremental pairwise value; Methods, Confound decomposition

strengths.text: The choice that could most easily have been fitted to the result was fixed in advance: layer 13 was pre-specified from an independent brain data set before any K562 perturbation data were examined, and the 18-layer profile is reported as a planned secondary analysis.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation; Methods, Perturbation-first validation

limitations.text: Two of the five contexts are too small to say anything. The iPSC neuron and T cell sets have 7 perturbations each, and the paper reports only a trend and a null for them, so the cross-context claim rests on K562 and RPE1.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Results, Cross-context replication; Discussion, Cross-context pattern

limitations.text: The numbers depend on choices that change them, and the gene universes differ between data sets. K562 uses 2,000 highly variable genes and RPE1 3,309 with the perturbed genes forced in, and the paper shows that restricting RPE1 to 2,000 genes changes the attention advantage by plus 0.168, so scores are not comparable across these settings.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Perturbation-first validation; Results, Cross-context replication

limitations.text: The endpoint is not regulation. The author states that this task is dominated by which genes are easy to detect as differentially expressed, and that the same attention edges do recover curated regulatory targets on the other objective, so a poor score here is not evidence that a model has learned nothing about regulation.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation and Positive control; Discussion, Endpoint-object mismatch

limitations.text: It is one author's evaluation of two models, with restrictive terms on the code. Only scGPT and Geneformer were tested, with newer single-cell models left for future work, and the repository's licence section asks that anyone wanting to reuse it contacts the author, although the Zenodo archive of the same release records a CC BY 4.0 licence.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Discussion, Limitations; README.md: License; Zenodo record 18701417 metadata

profile.summary: The GPN paper's own check of how well its DNA language model, trained on eight Brassicales genomes, predicts held-out Arabidopsis thaliana sequence and how well its embeddings separate gene regions. It reports test perplexity on a held-out chromosome, perplexity by position class in a 1-Mb test region, and a leave-one-chromosome-out classifier of gene regions from averaged embeddings. It is useful to plant genomics researchers comparing DNA language models on A. thaliana, but only the authors' own models are scored.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Training a Multispecies DNA Language Model', 'Unsupervised Clustering of Genomic Regions'; SI Appendix Table S2

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Two things about a masked DNA language model. First, how well it predicts nucleotides it has not seen, measured as perplexity on a held-out chromosome, genome-wide and in non-repeat regions, and by position class (splice sites, start and stop codons, codon positions, intergenic and intronic) in a 1-Mb test region. Second, whether its embeddings, learned without labels, carry gene structure: a classifier trained on embeddings averaged over 100-bp windows must assign each window to a gene region class.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Unsupervised Clustering of Genomic Regions' and 'DNA Motifs Revealed by High-Confidence Model Predictions'; Materials and Methods, 'Motif Analysis'

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The model was trained on 8 RefSeq-annotated Brassicales reference genomes. Arabidopsis thaliana chromosome 4 was held out for validation and chromosome 5 for testing. Training windows of 512 bp were drawn with emphasis on exons, promoters and an equal amount of random windows. For the embedding task, gene annotation came from EnsemblPlants; intergenic windows fully covered by repeats form a separate Repeat class, and windows with ambiguous annotation were dropped.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, 'Pretraining' and 'Analysis of Model Embeddings'

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Perplexity is the exponential of the cross-entropy loss; lower is better. Table S2 reports chromosome-wide and non-repeat test perplexity for three models that differ only in the loss weight on repeats. For gene regions, a scikit-learn logistic regression with inverse-frequency class weights and cross-validated L2 strength is trained on standardised window embeddings; each chromosome is predicted by a model trained on the others. The text reports per-class accuracy only for CDS (96%) and ncRNA (51%), and says k-mer frequency features do worse (SI Appendix, Figure S1).
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results and Materials and Methods, 'Analysis of Model Embeddings'; SI Appendix Table S2

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: The A. thaliana reference genome, with chromosome 5 as test set, the 1-Mb region Chr5:3,500,000-4,500,000 for position-class perplexity, and genome-wide 100-bp windows annotated from EnsemblPlants for gene region classification. The paper gives no window or position counts; the 1-Mb region contains 264 genes and 471 transcripts.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results and Materials and Methods

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Chromosome hold-out. For perplexity, A. thaliana chromosome 4 is validation and chromosome 5 is test. For gene region classification, each chromosome is predicted by a classifier trained on the remaining chromosomes.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, 'Pretraining' and 'Analysis of Model Embeddings'

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Perplexity (lower is better) for the sequence modelling tasks; per-class classification accuracy and a confusion matrix (higher accuracy is better) for gene region classification.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods; Figure 2B legend

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: GPN variants only: three repeat loss weights (1, 0.1 and 0) and a model trained on the A. thaliana genome alone, which had test perplexity 3.13 (3.17 on non-repeat regions). For gene regions, k-mer frequency features are the comparison (SI Appendix, Figure S1).
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, 'Pretraining'; SI Appendix Table S2

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Whole chromosomes are held out: chromosome 5 is never used in training, and the region classifier is evaluated leave-one-chromosome-out. The other seven training genomes are related species, and the paper does not discuss sequence shared between them and the test chromosome.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: None reported for the perplexities or accuracies: single values, no seeds or intervals.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results; SI Appendix Table S2

facts.label: Entity type
facts.value: A nucleotide position for perplexity; a 100-bp genomic window for gene region classification.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: Arabidopsis thaliana for evaluation; the training set adds seven other Brassicales species.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Training a Multispecies DNA Language Model'

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: No experimental assay: labels are the reference genome sequence itself and EnsemblPlants gene annotation.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, 'Analysis of Model Embeddings'

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence only: 512-bp windows of unaligned genomic sequence with masked positions.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Figure 1 legend

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Perplexity is zero-shot from the pretrained model. Gene region classification is a linear probe: logistic regression on frozen, averaged embeddings.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Unsupervised Clustering of Genomic Regions'

strengths.text: Test data are a whole held-out chromosome, and the region classifier is scored leave-one-chromosome-out, so test windows are not neighbours of training windows.
Perplexity is reported separately for non-repeat regions, so a reader can see the effect of repeats on the genome-wide figure.
The published model and the processed Arabidopsis data used by the study are on Hugging Face.

limitations.text: This is the authors' internal evaluation of their own models on one organism, Arabidopsis thaliana. No other DNA language model is scored, and there is no leaderboard.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Results; SI Appendix Table S2

limitations.text: The text gives only two per-class accuracies (CDS 96%, ncRNA 51%); the full confusion matrix is a figure. The authors note that ncRNA annotation errors may explain some confusion.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Unsupervised Clustering of Genomic Regions'

limitations.text: The paper's analysis code sits in an unmaintained archive that may depend on absolute paths and inputs that are no longer available.

name: GPN paper: unsupervised variant effect prediction in Arabidopsis thaliana
description: The paper's own evaluation of a genome-wide variant score in Arabidopsis thaliana, by enrichment of rare variants and of GWAS hits in the tail of the score distribution.

limitations: Author-defined and author-run.
The comparison against phyloP, phastCons, abs(phyloP) and LD Score is printed only as bar charts (Figures 5D, 6D, 6E and SI Appendix Figures S6, S8 to S12), so no comparator value is in this batch.
Rare versus common enrichment is a proxy for deleteriousness, not a measured functional effect.

review.method_note: Extraction: the published article prints no tables in its main text, so Table S2 was parsed from the pdftotext -layout text layer of the pinned SI Appendix PDF (extract/si-appendix.layout.txt) by extract/parse_values.py with all three row labels and the header asserted, and every other value was taken from the article body by matching its whole printed sentence in the pinned Europe PMC JATS XML, so a changed sentence fails the parse.
review.reviewer_note: Claude (Opus 5) extraction agent. Extraction only: no independent review is claimed, and a different agent reviews this batch.

attributes.scope_note: Arabidopsis thaliana only. There is no human variant evaluation anywhere in this paper. Enrichment is measured with Fisher's exact test on a two by two table of score class against variant class, so the endpoint is population genetic signal, not a curated pathogenic or benign label.
attributes.source_locator: Results, 'Unsupervised Variant Effect Prediction'; Materials and Methods, 'Variant Effect Prediction'
attributes.split: No train or test split: every variant in the set is scored by an unsupervised model
attributes.task: Unsupervised genome-wide variant effect prediction, scored by enrichment rather than against a labelled truth set

profile.summary: The GPN paper's own test of unsupervised, genome-wide variant effect prediction in Arabidopsis thaliana. A variant score is checked by whether its most extreme tail is enriched for rare variants in the 1001 Genomes data and for GWAS hits in the AraGWAS Catalog, using Fisher's exact test, with phyloP and phastCons conservation scores as comparators. There is no labelled truth set and no train or test split: the endpoint is population genetic signal.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Results, 'Unsupervised Variant Effect Prediction'; Materials and Methods, 'Variant Effect Prediction'

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a genome-wide variant score puts likely functional variants in its lowest tail. Three readouts are used: how variant consequence types rank under in silico mutagenesis of a 1-Mb region; enrichment of rare over common variants among the lowest-scoring 1001 Genomes SNPs; and enrichment of GWAS hits among the lowest-scoring AraGWAS variants. The paper scores variants with the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate to the reference allele.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Unsupervised Variant Effect Prediction'

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: In silico mutagenesis covers all possible SNPs in Chr5:3,500,000-4,500,000, annotated with Ensembl VEP; types with at least 1,000 variants are compared. The rare versus common set is over 10 million SNPs from the 1001 Genomes genotype matrix, where rare means allele count 1 and common means allele frequency above 5%. The GWAS set is AraGWAS summary statistics for 462 phenotypes (minimum allele count 6), with hits defined by the permutation-based threshold AraGWAS recommends, or by Bonferroni as a sensitivity check. The figure legend describes around half a million GWAS-tested variants.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, 'Variant Effect Prediction'; Figure 6 legend

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Each score is thresholded at a quantile (varied from 0.1% to 10%) to call variants putatively functional, and the odds ratio and P-value come from Fisher's exact test. Rare versus common is reported at the lowest 0.1%; GWAS enrichment at the lowest 1%. For GWAS, scores are also combined with linkage disequilibrium (GPN x LD, a weighted sum over squared correlations within 100 kb), and the same transform is applied to phyloP and phastCons; the unweighted LD Score is a baseline. When comparing with phyloP and phastCons, variants those scores cannot cover are excluded. In silico mutagenesis ranks variant consequence types by the first percentile of their GPN scores; a side analysis compares the share of repeat variants below the first missense decile across models with repeat loss weights 0, 0.1 and 1.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results; Materials and Methods, 'Variant Effect Prediction'

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Three sets: all possible SNPs in Chr5:3,500,000-4,500,000 (in silico mutagenesis); over 10 million 1001 Genomes SNPs (rare versus common); AraGWAS summary statistics for 462 phenotypes, around half a million tested variants (GWAS enrichment).
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results and Materials and Methods

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: None. Every variant is scored by an unsupervised model; the score's tail is compared with the rest. The model itself held out A. thaliana chromosome 5 in training, but the 1001 Genomes and GWAS analyses are genome-wide.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Odds ratio from Fisher's exact test (higher is better) for rare versus common and for GWAS hits. For in silico mutagenesis, the paper ranks consequence types by the first percentile of GPN scores, and separately compares the share of repeat variants below the first missense decile across repeat loss weights.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results; Materials and Methods

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: phyloP and phastCons conservation scores from 18 Brassicales species, abs(phyloP), their LD-weighted versions, the unweighted LD Score, GPN models with other repeat weights, and a GPN trained on A. thaliana alone.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results; Materials and Methods

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Not applicable in the usual sense: no labels are used in training. The paper does not discuss whether population allele frequencies or GWAS results relate to the model's training genomes.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Fisher's exact test P-values accompany the odds ratios; no confidence intervals, seeds or replicates are given in the text.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, 'Variant Effect Prediction'

facts.label: Entity type
facts.value: A single-nucleotide variant.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: Arabidopsis thaliana only.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Population genotyping (1001 Genomes allele counts and frequencies) and genome-wide association studies (AraGWAS); consequence labels from Ensembl VEP. No functional assay.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Any genome-wide variant score. GPN uses sequence context only; the comparators use whole-genome alignments, and the GWAS scores add an LD matrix.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Zero-shot: scores come from the pretrained model with no training on labels.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, 'Variant Effect Prediction'

strengths.text: Genome-wide: coding and non-coding variants are scored on one scale and judged against the same population and GWAS signals.
Results are reported across thresholds from 0.1% to 10% and with two GWAS significance rules, so a reader can see how much a result depends on the cut-off.

review.method_note: Independent review pass of 2026-11-16. All four pinned artifacts were re-retrieved. The Nature article PDF, the Supplementary Information PDF and the Hugging Face collection API JSON each hashed to the value on their source record. The bioRxiv PDF did not and cannot: two downloads minutes apart gave b3e4d729d3363c16fb6b6cb99e4e18ffadb01b48614dba910480fb96f42b3d73 and 47f87f72baf93793177d3e40f70f43f03ac5d3050bbc5244f655e92041c7db4a, differing from each other in 34 bytes, all of them download-time stamps (XMP ModifyDate and MetadataDate, the xmpMM DocumentID and InstanceID, the document /ModDate and the second element of the trailer /ID); the page count, the CreationDate of 2025-09-21 and the pdftotext -layout text layer are identical across downloads. No value in this batch comes from the preprint. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly: 12 in_cell, 44 in_row, 16 locator_not_parsed, no not_in_row, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row (value-check.tsv). All 72 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build.py. Supplementary Table 3 is printed rotated, so that script reads the page's word bounding boxes rather than a text dump: it recovers the seven column bands from the header words' y extents, pairing each 'Finemapped' header with whichever of 'coding' and 'non-coding' overlaps it, clusters the body words into eight row bands by x centre, and places every numeric token in the cell whose column centre is nearest, rejecting any token that is more than 45 per cent of a column pitch from its nearest column or less than 25 per cent of a pitch clear of the runner-up. Column order is therefore a measured property of the page and not an assumption, which is the check extract/build.py could not make: it asserted the column order positionally. Results are matched to cells through each source_locator's text, not through record IDs. Fig. 4b's 12 bar labels were required to be the first number printed after their series label on the same line, and the four rare variant counts were matched against the two sentences that print them, with the capture position fixing which count belongs to DeepRVAT with GPN-Star annotations and which to the original method. Result: 68 in cell, 4 in sentence, 0 failures (review/value-check-independent.tsv). Two negative controls confirm the checker is a cell check and not a row check: exchanging two ClinVar values between rows and moving a Fig. 4b label onto another series both fail (review/control-swap.tsv), and shifting a value into a neighbouring column of its own row fails and names the column that actually holds it, including across the Finemapped coding / OMIM and Finemapped coding / Finemapped non-coding boundaries (review/control-shift.tsv). Independently of both scripts, all 56 cells of Supplementary Table 3 and all 12 Fig. 4b labels were transcribed by hand from the pages rendered at 190 dpi with pdftoppm, into review/manual-transcription.tsv, and compared by review/cmp_manual.py: 68 values, 0 problems. That hand pass is what settles the column assignment the repository checker could only place at row level. The 12 descriptive claims were read against the pinned PDFs and the collection JSON.

attributes.task: Genome-wide variant effect (functional constraint) prediction

profile.summary: These are the variant effect prediction benchmarks the GPN-Star authors assembled to evaluate their alignment- and phylogeny-aware genomic language model. Seven classification tasks pit curated pathogenic or causal variants against common or non-causal controls (ClinVar and COSMIC missense, OMIM and HGMD non-coding, UK Biobank fine-mapped coding and non-coding, and promoter variants), scored by area under the precision-recall curve; a deep mutational scanning task reports Spearman correlation on 31 human protein assays; and two further tasks measure gnomAD rare versus common enrichment and gene discovery in rare variant association testing. The benchmark datasets are published on Hugging Face, so the comparison is reusable even though the paper's own role was to show one model.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Fig. 2 caption; Results; Data availability. Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a genome-wide score separates variants that matter from variants that do not, across the settings where that question is asked in practice. Coding: pathogenic against benign missense in ClinVar, cancer-frequent against population-common missense in COSMIC, and fitness measured by deep mutational scanning. Non-coding: curated pathogenic regulatory variants from OMIM and HGMD against common controls, and fine-mapped GWAS variants with high against low posterior inclusion probability. Then two uses rather than classifications: whether the score's deleterious tail is enriched for rare gnomAD variants, and whether adding the score as an annotation finds more genes in rare variant association testing.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, Pathogenic coding variants, Pathogenic non-coding variants, Fine-mapped variants in GWAS, Rare variant association testing, Genome-wide evolutionary constraints. Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Each task reuses a published resource at a stated version and, for the non-coding tasks, a matched control design taken from TraitGym. ClinVar is release 20220924, pathogenic against benign missense. COSMIC frequent mutations are those in more than 0.1% of whole-genome or whole-exome samples in MutantCensus v98, against gnomAD common missense. ProteinGym contributes 31 human protein assays from v0.1, restricted to amino acid substitutions reachable by a single nucleotide change, taking the most deleterious such change by CADD. For OMIM and HGMD, each pathogenic variant is matched with nine control variants on chromosome, molecular consequence and distance to the transcription start site; for fine-mapped non-coding variants the matching adds LD score and minor allele frequency, while for fine-mapped coding variants only allele frequency is matched. The gnomAD task uses v3.1.2 allele frequencies and follows the GPN-MSA protocol: the deleterious tail is cut at the threshold giving 30 false discoveries and rare variants are subsampled to the number of common variants in each consequence category.
sections.source_locator: Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks, Datasets

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: AUPRC on the complete benchmark set, with 95% confidence intervals from 1,000 class-stratified bootstrap resamples, for the seven classification tasks; Spearman correlation per assay for ProteinGym, shown as a distribution over the 31 assays. One rule keeps the comparison fair across many models: for each benchmark only variants for which every compared model has a prediction are used. The rare variant association testing experiment runs DeepRVAT on 34 UK Biobank quantitative traits using whole-exome data from 161,822 unrelated individuals of European ancestry, keeping variants below 0.1% minor allele frequency, with and without the three GPN-Star scores as added annotations, repeated three times with different random seeds; the outcome is the number of significant genes at family-wise error rate below 0.05 and how many of those replicate in larger published studies.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Fig. 2 caption; Results, Rare variant association testing. Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks

sections.title: The models compared
sections.body: The comparison set is unusually wide and is pinned in the supplementary methods: classical conservation scores PhyloP and PhastCons at three evolutionary timescales, the ensemble CADD v1.7 raw scores, single-sequence genomic language models Nucleotide Transformer 2.5B multispecies and Evo 2 at 7B and 40B with an 8,192 base pair context, the earlier alignment model GPN-MSA, protein language models ESM-1b, ESM-2 and ESM-3-open, the sequence-to-function models Enformer, Borzoi and AlphaGenome, the allele-frequency-informed AlphaMissense and PrimateAI-3D, the promoter-specific PromoterAI, SpeciesLM and GPN-Promoter, and Roulette mutation rate estimates. Most scores were taken precomputed from the original authors or from TraitGym rather than recomputed.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results; Extended Data Fig. 1 caption. Supplementary Information: Compared models

sections.title: Reported results
sections.body: The paper reports GPN-Star first on every benchmark. On ClinVar missense, GPN-Star (V) has the highest AUPRC, matching ESM-1b and beating ESM-2 and ESM-3-open. On OMIM and HGMD non-coding variants GPN-Star (M) is best, and the sequence-to-function models do substantially worse than alignment-based and phylogenetic models. On fine-mapped coding variants GPN-Star (M) leads, with AlphaMissense and PrimateAI-3D substantially outperformed despite their use of allele frequency; on fine-mapped non-coding variants it leads again, with Evo 2 of limited value. On promoter variants it beats the promoter-specific models by a wide margin. Adding all three GPN-Star scores to DeepRVAT raised the significant gene count from 383 to 402 on average and the replicating subset from 338 to 353. No cross-model score is printed in text form; the AUPRC values for competing models are only in Fig. 2 and Extended Data Fig. 1. For reference, the ablation table in the Supplementary Information (Supplementary Table 3), which compares GPN-Star architecture variants trained the same way rather than competing models, gives the default GPN-Star architecture (mean of three initialisations) 0.896 on ClinVar, 0.391 on COSMIC, 0.383 on ProteinGym, 0.239 on fine-mapped coding, 0.713 on OMIM, 0.222 on fine-mapped non-coding and 0.570 on HGMD.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, Pathogenic coding variants, Pathogenic non-coding variants, Fine-mapped variants in GWAS, Rare variant association testing. Supplementary Information: Supplementary Table 3

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The benchmark datasets, the pretrained models and the whole-genome alignments are published in one Hugging Face collection, and precomputed GPN-Star scores for every possible single nucleotide variant in the human genome and five model organisms are released separately. The code to train, run inference and reproduce the main analyses is on GitHub with a Zenodo archive. To score a new model on these benchmarks a user needs the dataset repositories from the collection, for example clinvar_vs_benign, cosmic, omim_traitgym, ukb_finemapped_coding, ukb_finemapped_nc_traitgym and gnomad_balanced, and should apply the paper's rule of keeping only variants that every compared model can score.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Data availability and Code availability. Hugging Face collection record: items. Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Ten tasks over eight sources: ClinVar release 20220924 (pathogenic against benign missense), COSMIC MutantCensus v98 against gnomAD v3 common missense, ProteinGym v0.1 restricted to 31 human protein assays, OMIM and HGMD curated pathogenic regulatory variants against gnomAD common controls at nine controls per positive, UK Biobank fine-mapped variants across 65 traits (coding) and 83 traits (non-coding), promoter subsets of the OMIM and fine-mapped sets, gnomAD v3.1.2 allele frequencies, and UK Biobank whole-exome data for 34 quantitative traits. The variant counts per benchmark are printed only in the figure panel headings, which are images, so no count is recorded here.
facts.source_locator: Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks, Datasets. Paper: Fig. 2 caption; Results

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Two different things are split here. The benchmarks themselves are evaluated whole, with no train and test division, because the scores are zero-shot; the structure comes from the matched control design (nine controls per positive for OMIM, HGMD and fine-mapped non-coding, matched on chromosome, consequence and distance to the transcription start site, plus LD score and allele frequency for the latter, and allele frequency only for fine-mapped coding). The model's own training split keeps chromosomes 1 to 20, X and Y for training, chromosome 21 for validation and chromosome 22 as the held-out test chromosome, which is the chromosome used for the gnomAD allele frequency analyses.
facts.source_locator: Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks, Supplementary Table 1. Paper: Results, Genome-wide evolutionary constraints

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: AUPRC for the seven classification benchmarks, higher better, computed on the complete benchmark set with 95% bootstrap intervals. Spearman correlation per assay for ProteinGym, higher better. For the gnomAD analysis, enrichment of rare over common variants in the deleterious tail at a threshold giving 30 false discoveries, higher better, plus mean minor allele frequency by quantile bin. For rare variant association testing, the number of significant genes at family-wise error rate below 0.05 and the number replicating larger studies, higher better.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Fig. 2 and Fig. 4 captions; Results. Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks and Supplementary Table 3

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: PhyloP and PhastCons at vertebrate, mammal and primate timescales; CADD v1.7; GPN-MSA; Nucleotide Transformer 2.5B multispecies; Evo 2 at 7B and 40B; ESM-1b, ESM-2 and ESM-3-open; Enformer, Borzoi and AlphaGenome; AlphaMissense and PrimateAI-3D; PromoterAI, SpeciesLM and GPN-Promoter; and Roulette mutation rate estimates. Scores were largely taken precomputed from the original publications or from TraitGym.
facts.source_locator: Supplementary Information: Compared models. Paper: Results; Extended Data Fig. 1 caption

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Several, and one acknowledged conflict. Chromosome 22 is held out of the model's training and is the chromosome used for the gnomAD analyses. Controls are matched to positives on chromosome, consequence and distance to the transcription start site, and for fine-mapped variants also on LD score and allele frequency, so a score cannot win by exploiting location or frequency. Only variants scored by every compared model are included. The authors also note the opposite problem for two comparators: AlphaMissense and PrimateAI-3D use human population allele frequencies in training and so gain an advantage on ClinVar, where allele frequency defines the benign class, and they report a frequency-adjusted variant of their own model alongside. Nothing is said about whether the ClinVar or HGMD variants themselves influenced any model's training corpus beyond that.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Genome-wide evolutionary constraints. Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks; Supplementary Figure 1 caption

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: 95% confidence intervals from 1,000 class-stratified bootstrap resamples on every AUPRC, and a boxplot over 31 assays for ProteinGym showing median, mean, quartiles and whiskers. The rare variant association testing experiment is repeated with three random seeds and reported as an average with each initialisation plotted. The ablation table reports the mean and the maximum over three random initialisations. No significance tests between models are reported.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Fig. 2 caption; Results, Rare variant association testing. Supplementary Information: Supplementary Table 3 caption

facts.label: Entity type
facts.value: One single nucleotide variant in the human genome for the classification and enrichment tasks, with its molecular consequence from Ensembl VEP under the most severe consequence rule. For ProteinGym the unit scored is a variant but the reported value is one Spearman correlation per assay. For rare variant association testing the unit is a gene and trait pair.
facts.source_locator: Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks. Paper: Fig. 2 caption; Results, Rare variant association testing

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: Human for all ten tasks on this record. The wider paper also evaluates models for mouse, chicken, fruit fly, nematode and Arabidopsis against pathogenic or lethal variant sets, but those are separate benchmarks.
facts.source_locator: Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks, Homo sapiens. Paper: Results, GPN-Star for model organisms

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Only one task rests on a measurement: ProteinGym's deep mutational scanning fitness scores for 31 human proteins. The other labels are database annotations or statistical inferences: expert curation in ClinVar, OMIM and HGMD, sample frequency in COSMIC, posterior inclusion probability from GWAS fine-mapping, and population allele frequency in gnomAD.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Fig. 2 caption; Results. Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Unrestricted in practice: the benchmarks compare whatever each model reads. The model under test uses whole-genome alignments and a species tree rather than a single sequence, the comparators range from single-sequence genomic language models to protein language models, sequence-to-function models trained on functional genomics data, and methods that use human population allele frequencies. The one constraint applied is that a model must produce a score for a variant for that variant to count.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Results. Supplementary Information: Compared models and Evaluation Benchmarks

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Zero-shot for the classification and correlation benchmarks: scores are model likelihoods or published conservation and ensemble scores, with no fitting to the benchmark labels. Two exceptions sit on top of the scores: a logistic regression used for the embedding classification analyses under leave-one-chromosome-out cross-validation, and the rare variant association testing, where the GPN-Star scores are fed as annotations into DeepRVAT, which is itself trained.
facts.source_locator: Supplementary Information: embedding analysis. Paper: Results, Rare variant association testing

strengths.text: The control design is matched rather than random: nine controls per positive, matched on chromosome, consequence and distance to the transcription start site, with LD score and allele frequency added for fine-mapped non-coding variants, which removes the easiest shortcuts on non-coding tasks.

The comparison is run on the same variant sets for every model, with the explicit rule that a variant counts only if all compared models can score it, and the models are pinned with versions and score provenance in the supplementary methods.
strengths.source_locator: Supplementary Information: Evaluation Benchmarks and Compared models

strengths.text: The benchmark datasets themselves are released, not just the results: the Hugging Face collection holds the per-task datasets alongside the models and alignments, and the analysis code is archived on Zenodo.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Data availability and Code availability. Hugging Face collection record: items

strengths.text: An unfair advantage held by two comparators is stated rather than hidden: AlphaMissense and PrimateAI-3D use allele frequency in training while ClinVar's benign class is defined by allele frequency, and the authors add a frequency-adjusted version of their own model for that comparison.

limitations.text: The benchmarks were assembled by the authors of the model that wins them, and the paper reports GPN-Star as best or joint best on every task.

The numbers are in pictures. The AUPRC values and the per-benchmark sample sizes appear only in the Fig. 2 and Extended Data Fig. 1 panels and their headings, so a reader cannot take a model's score, or a benchmark's size, from the text. The only per-benchmark figures in text form are in the ablation table, which compares architecture variants rather than competing models.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Fig. 2 caption; Extended Data Fig. 1 caption. Supplementary Information: Supplementary Table 3 caption

limitations.text: Two of the label sources are not released with the benchmark or are frozen in time: HGMD data were obtained already curated from another study (ref. 91) rather than released with this benchmark, and ClinVar is release 20220924, so the ClinVar task reflects curation as of September 2022.

The rare variant association testing result is a small average difference under a design that cannot be rerun by most readers: 402 against 383 significant genes and 353 against 338 replicating, averaged over three seeds, on UK Biobank exome data for 161,822 individuals of European ancestry, which is controlled-access and one ancestry group only.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Results, Rare variant association testing

run_guide.summary: Get the published benchmark datasets and the precomputed scores from Hugging Face, and the analysis code from GitHub, then score a model on the same variants under the paper's inclusion rule.
prerequisites: A Hugging Face client or the datasets library to pull the collection's dataset repositories.
The gpn code from GitHub, or its Zenodo archive, for training, inference and the analysis scripts.
For the HGMD benchmark, access to the curated HGMD data, which the supplementary methods obtain from a third party rather than release.
For the rare variant association testing experiment, controlled access to UK Biobank whole-exome data.
The article is CC BY 4.0; no licence for the benchmark dataset repositories was read.

steps.title: Get the analysis code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/songlab-cal/gpn.git
cd gpn
steps.explanation: The repository named in the paper's code availability statement, which says it holds the code to train, run inference and reproduce the main analyses. No commit is pinned here because the sources read name only the repository and its Zenodo archive.

steps.title: Download the benchmark datasets
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from datasets import load_dataset

for name in [
    "songlab/clinvar_vs_benign",
    "songlab/cosmic",
    "songlab/omim_traitgym",
    "songlab/ukb_finemapped_coding",
    "songlab/ukb_finemapped_nc_traitgym",
    "songlab/gnomad_balanced",
]:
    ds = load_dataset(name)
    print(name, ds)
PY
steps.explanation: The dataset repository names are the items of the Hugging Face collection that the paper's data availability statement points to as holding the benchmark datasets. The loading loop is written here; the sources read give no loading example of their own.
steps.source_locator: Paper: Data availability. Hugging Face collection record: items

steps.title: Get the precomputed GPN-Star scores to compare against
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from datasets import load_dataset

ds = load_dataset("songlab/gpn-star-scores")
print(ds)
PY
steps.explanation: The paper releases precomputed predictions for every possible single nucleotide variant in the human genome and the five model organisms; the collection lists that dataset repository as gpn-star-scores. Scoring a new model means producing its own score for the same variants and then, following the paper, keeping only variants that every compared model can score.

name: CACHE Challenge #3
description: Blinded prospective community challenge in which computational teams select commercially available compounds for a named target, the organisers synthesise and assay them, and confirmed hits are scored by an independent Hit Evaluation Committee.

attributes.task: Prospective hit identification for the SARS-CoV-2 Nsp3 macrodomain (Mac1)
attributes.scope_note: Round 1 (hit identification): each of 23 workflows selected up to 100 commercially available compounds; 1739 were synthesised by Enamine and tested. All 1739 were screened at 100 uM by homogeneous time-resolved fluorescence (HTRF); 302 reduced the binding signal by 30% or more in at least one of two duplicates or gave ambiguous data and went to a limited three-point dose response, then to surface plasmon resonance; 28 advanced to Round 2. In parallel all 1739 were soaked with crystallised Nsp3-Mac1, giving complex structures for 44. Round 2 (hit expansion): up to 50 close analogues per team, 296 compounds tested, 84 confirmed. Teams were also asked to predict actives from the merged library of all 1739 Round 1 compounds, so that every workflow ran on the same library; confirmed hits with a score above 15 were clustered into four chemically novel Tier 1 compounds and 25 Tier 2 compounds.
attributes.source_locator: Results 'Compounds Were Drug-like and Chemically Diverse', 'Discovering Chemically Novel Ligands Was Challenging', 'Selection and Experimental Testing of Round 2 Compounds'; Figure 6 caption
limitations: The challenge scores confirmed hits with an activity score set by a Hit Evaluation Committee and a novelty score voted by three chemists. It does not publish a per-workflow hit rate.

Targets and libraries were chosen by the organisers and predictions were submitted before testing, so there is no training-overlap control in the usual sense; the Nsp3-Mac1 binding features were already well documented, and 61 Mac1 ligands had been published.
Only the published CACHE #3 round is extracted here. The CACHE #1 and #2 results papers (doi 10.1021/acs.jcim.4c01267 and 10.1021/acs.jcim.5c00535) are not open access and were not retrieved.
